title: Contractor to Full-Time Conversion Guide
author: Elena Rossi
content:
> **Archived 2026-03-05:** this page is superseded by "Role Transition Playbook: Embedded Contractor to Full-Time Conversion" and is kept for reference only.

Overview:
This guide describes how Redwood Inference converts embedded contractors, consultants and long-running vendor staff into full-time employees (FTEs). It walks through approvals, onboarding (technical and cultural), competency checkpoints, IT/security provisioning, compensation calibration and a 90-day ramp to role parity. The aim is a predictable conversion that keeps delivery stable and preserves our security and compliance posture.

When this guide applies:
- A contractor has accepted a formal offer to move into an FTE role.
- A long-term vendor engagement is being brought in-house as internal headcount.
- A team has requested a full-time role to take over work currently done by a contractor.

Key objectives:
- Finish HR and security provisioning before the person's first day as an FTE.
- Have at least 3 documented artifacts and 1 knowledge-transfer session in place before the role transfers.
- Hit competency checkpoints at day 30, 60 and 90.

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager: sponsors the conversion, sets role expectations, runs the technical and cultural assessment, and owns the 90-day ramp plan.
- People Ops: coordinates the offer, background checks, compensation calibration and new-hire admin.
- IT/Security: validates access changes and approves privileged access before the start date.
- Finance: assigns the budget code and payroll start date.
- Peer Sponsor (Buddy): chosen by the hiring manager to give day-to-day operational support for the first 45 days.

Pre-offer checklist (Hiring Manager & People Ops):
1) Confirm headcount and budget with Finance.
2) Check contractor status, IP clauses and any non-compete implications with Legal.
3) Confirm benefits eligibility and any relocation needs.
4) Calibrate the compensation band against the banding matrix and recent benchmarks.
5) Draft the offer letter and a proposed start date.

Offer and acceptance (People Ops):
- Standard timeline: 5 business days for initial offer response window.
- The offer states start date, compensation, title, reporting manager, benefits overview, probation period (where relevant) and any relocation/visa contingencies.
- On acceptance, People Ops kicks off the background check, payroll onboarding form, corporate email reservation and badge request.

Security and legal gating (before start):
- Background check cleared.
- IP assignment signed and the contractor agreement terminated or amended.
- Vendor/third-party agreements reviewed so data ownership and access policies carry over.
- MFA and SSO provisioning scheduled.

Technical and operational handoff (Hiring Manager and Peer Sponsor):
- Artifact inventory covering code repos, runbooks, dashboards, deployment keys and vendor accounts, with links and owners.
- 1x knowledge-transfer session documented (recording or written notes).
- An access de-escalation plan where contractor credentials must be retired.
- 30/60/90 deliverables tied to an objective success metric (templates below).

First-week checklist (Day 0-7):
- HR: benefits orientation, payroll confirmation, paperwork.
- IT: laptop assigned, VPN/SSO access, standard toolchain installed.
- Security: any privileged access exceptions validated and logged.
- Manager: daily check-ins, buddy pairing, review of expectations and success metrics.
- Team: welcome intro, stakeholder directory, recurring meeting invites.

30/60/90 day milestones (adapt by role):
- 30 days: onboarding tasks done, at least one reviewed end-to-end change or deliverable shipped, key cross-team syncs attended, basic runbook walk-through passed.
- 60 days: delivers recurring tasks independently, owns one operational area (e.g., monitoring or deploys), contributes to planning.
- 90 days: at parity with peers on productivity and quality; leads a small project and mentors others on the transferred knowledge.

Role parity assessment (day 90):
- Technical proficiency: practical review of PRs, feature ownership and incident participation.
- Process adoption: uses team workflows, ticketing, CI/CD and observability tooling.
- Collaboration: part of team rituals, communicates well with stakeholders, positive feedback from buddy and partners.

Compensation and benefits notes:
- Conversions within 6 months: standard band review; manager justifies any above-band offer.
- Conversions after 12+ months: attach a performance summary and manager endorsement if accelerated banding is requested.
- Equity eligibility is confirmed at offer time per People Ops policy, with the vesting start date set in the offer.

Example 30-day deliverables:
1) Engineer: "Ship a small bugfix or feature with automated tests and an updated deployment runbook."
2) Product manager: "Write a 1-page customer problem brief and run the first prioritization triage."
3) Designer: "Produce a prototype with usability notes and present it to cross-functional partners."

Access and credentialing:
- Replace vendor-managed credentials with new corporate credentials; never carry over shared secrets.
- Rotate keys or tokens used during the contractor period on day 0 of FTE status.
- For sensitive systems, grant limited access on day 1 and expand after the 30-day review.

Buddy guidance (Peer Sponsor):
- Time allocation: 1 hour/day for the first 2 weeks, then 1-2 hours/week through week 6.
- Activities: guided walkthroughs, shadowing deploys, calendar clean-up, culture Q&A.
- Buddies write a short onboarding summary at day 30.

Risk controls and exceptions:
- If the contractor touched customer data, audit prior access and re-certify before conversion.
- Unresolved IP or contract obligations block offer finalization.
- For visa-sponsored contractors, involve immigration counsel early and do not fix a start date until the visa transfer is confirmed.

Manager checklist (90 days):
- Week 1: paperwork confirmed, buddy assigned, access validated, first deliverable scoped.
- Weeks 2-4: weekly 1:1s on knowledge gaps and artifact completion.
- Month 2: 30/60 progress review with People Ops.
- Month 3: 90-day parity review and sign-off; agree any ongoing development plan.

Records and audit trail:
- People Ops keeps the conversion packet (offer, background check confirmation, IP assignment, role activation) in HRIS.
- The Hiring Manager uploads the artifact inventory and buddy summary to the team onboarding folder and links it to the HR packet.

Escalation:
- Notify Security and People Ops immediately about critical access or security issues; pause the conversion if needed.
- Compensation disputes are mediated by People Ops and Finance, with final approval by the Head of People.

Revision history:
- 2025-08-19: Created
